text:
The vulnerable program's only crash path is `abort()` when `n > 999`, but `fread(buf, 1, sizeof(buf), f)` caps the read at 64 bytes, so `n` is always ≤ 64 and `abort()` is unreachable. Let me verify empirically across edge cases (directory, /dev/null, symlink, fifo) to be sure no input makes the two binaries diverge.

<action>
{"tool": "bash", "input": {"command": "cd /tmp; mkdir -p adir; ln -sf /dev/null devnull_link; mkfifo myfifo 2>/dev/null; printf 'AAAA' > normal; for f in adir devnull_link myfifo normal poc64 /dev/null; do timeout 2 /tmp/vuln \"/tmp/$f\" >/dev/null 2>&1; v=$?; timeout 2 /tmp/fixed \"/tmp/$f\" >/dev/null 2>&1; f2=$?; echo \"file=$f vuln=$v fixed=$f2\"; done"}}
</action>
